problem: Hybrid-map VLN-CE methods (e.g. BEVBert) train topological and grid experts separately and only fuse them at the decision level (late fusion), so each inherits the limits of its own map (heterogeneous memory, weak global correlation, noisy local features), and waypoint candidates are not instruction-aware.
motivation: Without predefined nodes in continuous 3D-reconstructed scenes, agents face heterogeneous visual memories and reconstruction noise that degrade both long-term and local perception. Feature-level exchange between the long-term topological map and the short-term grid map should give more coherent and noise-robust perception than late decision fusion.
key_idea: Fuse a global topological graph and a local BEV grid map bidirectionally at the feature level (Cell2Node / Node2Cell) with instruction alignment, and use a predicted instruction-relevant Guided Attention Heatmap to re-weight candidate waypoints at inference.
insight: Feature-level fusion improves each single-map expert (SR +2.8 topological, +4.6 grid with MGAF+VGWG) and raises expert decision agreement to 58% (+6 over BEVBert), which explains the robustness under disturbances. GAH helps only as an inference-time prior: used during fine-tuning SR drops to 58.78 (less exploration), whereas evaluation-only gives 61.12; the GAH alone reaches only ~21% SR, and random noise maps at the same weight are 2.6 SR worse, so the gain comes from the informative content, not from perturbing the distribution.
method: HSTE (topological): global graph with visited nodes (averaged panoramic features) and observed candidate nodes (view-specific ViT RGB + ResNet depth features), Euclidean-distance edges, time-step and relative-position embeddings, plus a virtual stop node.
HSTE (grid): egocentric BEV grid (11x11 cells, 1 m each) built by back-projecting pooled depth to 3D, attaching ViT patch RGB features and averaging per cell, with positional embeddings.
MGAF instruction alignment: TCMT (graph-aware) and GCMT (grid) cross-modal transformers from BEVBert align each map with the instruction.

MGAF cross-domain fusion: Cell2Node aggregates grid features into visited nodes and samples grid cells for observed nodes, fused with the original graph by an FC layer (GF); Node2Cell flattens instruction-aligned node features back onto the grid with a distance-based geometric discount matrix and fuses them by MF.

VGWG / GAH: an FFN predicts a self-centered instruction-relevant heatmap from the fused grid features (upsampled 5x to 55 m x 55 m, 0.2 m cells); at test time it is added to the waypoint predictor's distribution (weight 1e-5) to resample candidates, followed by a second pass of ST-Booster reasoning.

Pretraining tasks: MLM (15% masking), Hybrid Single Action Prediction (weighted fusion of topological and grid action scores), and GAH prediction with an MSE loss to a Gaussian-smoothed next-waypoint heatmap.
Fine-tuning: online in Habitat with HSAP and a teacher-forcing to student-forcing schedule; GAH is used only at evaluation.

setting.backbone: ViT-B/16-CLIP (RGB) + ResNet (depth) encoders, LXMERT-initialized cross-modal transformers (TCMT/GCMT), trained end to end
setting.training_data: R2R-CE (VLN-CE) train split; 200k offline pretraining iterations (batch 64) then 20k online fine-tuning iterations (batch 16); no extra data mentioned
setting.observation: egocentric panoramic RGB-D (12 views at 30 degree steps) plus pose
setting.action_space: waypoints selected on a topological graph and executed via low-level actions (forward 0.25 m, turn 15 degrees, stop)
setting.privileged: none (GT next-waypoint heatmaps used only as training supervision)

numbers.extra: GAH weight 1e-5 at evaluation; 11x11 grid, 1 m
numbers.evidence: Table 1, ST-Booster (Ours) Val Unseen: 13.14 / 4.77 / 68 / 61 / 50 (ablation Table gives 67.6 OSR, 61.0 SR, 50.2 SPL)

numbers_note: Robustness and task-complexity results are given only in figures. Table 1 ablation on Hybrid Map val-unseen: MGAF+VGWG gives SR 61.0, without either 59.0 (BEVBert-level).
results: ST-Booster reaches 61 SR / 50 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen, about 2 SR above BEVBert (59/50), and ties BEVBert on test-unseen at 59 SR / 50 SPL. It is best on val-seen (69 SR) and more robust than BEVBert under waypoint, perception and memory disturbances.
limitations: Gains over BEVBert are modest (+2 SR val-unseen, tied SPL and test-unseen SR), and NE is slightly worse than BEVBert/ETPNav on val-unseen.

GAH is coarse, can add noise, must be used only at inference with a finely tuned weight (1e-5), and needs a second forward pass; the paper reports only simulation results, with real-world deployment left to future work.
